title: Sequential Topological Superconductivity in a Square Lattice with Chiral Charge Density Waves
authors: Zhong-Xian Jin, Junkang Huang, Yu-Xuan Li, Tao Zhou
abstract: The interplay between charge order and superconductivity offers a fertile ground for emergent quantum phases. Here we theoretically investigate a square-lattice superconductor coexisting with a composite charge density wave (CDW) consisting of a real bond modulation (charge bond order, CBO) and an imaginary hopping modulation (chiral flux phase, CFP) that breaks time-reversal symmetry. We uncover that, while CFP alone does not induce topology in square lattices, its coexistence with CBO drives the system into two topologically nontrivial superconducting phases with Chern numbers $C=+2$ and $C=-2$. The low-temperature thermal Hall conductivity $κ_{xy}$ exhibits quantized plateaus proportional to the Chern number, providing a clear experimental fingerprint. Our results establish the square lattice as a pristine platform for engineering topological superconductivity through the synergy of real and imaginary bond modulations.
summary: This work theoretically explores how the combination of real and imaginary bond modulations within a square lattice superconductor induces sequential transitions into topologically non-trivial superconducting phases. By calculating the Chern number and predicting quantized thermal Hall conductivity plateaus, the authors establish this platform as a robust method for engineering topological superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates topological superconducting phases arising from the interplay between superconductivity and a composite Charge Density Wave (CDW) in a square lattice.
main_result: The coexistence of real bond modulation (CBO) and imaginary hopping modulation (CFP) drives the system into two distinct, topologically nontrivial superconducting phases characterized by Chern numbers $C=+2$ and $C=-2$.
method: Theoretical analysis using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian in momentum space, calculating topological invariants like the Chern number via the Kubo formula.
model_or_system: The model is a square-lattice superconductor subjected to a composite CDW consisting of CBO ($\lambda_{	ext{CBO}}$) and CFP ($\lambda_{	ext{CFP}}$). The Hamiltonian is analyzed in the Altland-Zirnbauer class D, breaking time-reversal symmetry.
key_observables: Quantized plateaus in the zero-temperature thermal Hall conductivity ($\kappa_{xy} \propto C$), Chern number ($C$), and gapless edge modes observed via spectral function analysis.
important_parameters: The relative strengths of $\lambda_{	ext{CBO}}$ and $\lambda_{	ext{CFP}}$, chemical potential ($\mu$), and temperature (analyzed in the zero-temperature limit).
main_assumptions: The superconducting pairing is assumed to be an isotropic s-wave form, and the analysis relies on diagonalizing the BdG Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures schematically show the real-space CDW pattern (CBO/CFP) and illustrate topological phase diagrams showing transitions between $C=-2, 0, 2$ phases as parameters are varied.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the Hamiltonian incorporating CBO and CFP, analyzing the resulting band structure evolution through different parameter regimes, determining the topological invariants ($C$) at critical points via gap closing mechanisms (quadratic vs. linear touching), and finally predicting observable signatures like quantized $\kappa_{xy}$.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between engineered charge order parameters (CDW) and robust topological superconductivity provides a concrete theoretical pathway for realizing exotic quantum states, which is highly relevant to understanding unconventional pairing mechanisms in correlated materials.
